title: Logic Optimization Meets SAT: A Novel Framework for Circuit-SAT Solving
problem: Circuit Satisfiability (CSAT) problems are critical in IC design and verification but existing SAT solvers optimized for CNF struggle with circuit structure intrinsics. Direct CSAT conversion to CNF loses structural information that could accelerate solving.
motivation: CSAT instances capture real circuit verification tasks but generic CNF solvers cannot exploit circuit topology, creating unnecessary inefficiency in design verification workflows.
method: The approach preprocesses circuit satisfiability problems using logic synthesis—techniques to restructure and simplify circuits. It applies lookup-table mapping, which transforms the circuit logic into simplified forms easier for SAT solvers to work with, guided by a reinforcement learning agent that learns which specific transformations produce the fastest solutions. Rather than using the same strategy for all problems, the RL agent customizes its transformation approach for each circuit instance.
key_novelty: Reinforcement learning optimizes circuit preprocessing strategies (via lookup-table mapping) for each problem instance, learning which transformations yield the fastest SAT solving.
contributions: Preprocessing framework combining logic synthesis and reinforcement learning
Cost-customized LUT mapping strategy tailored for SAT solver efficiency
RL agent for adaptive transformation selection per instance
63% runtime reduction on industrial-scale CSAT benchmarks vs conventional approaches

metrics.speedup: 63% runtime reduction vs conventional CSAT-to-CNF approaches

limitations: RL training overhead on initial instances and applicability to parallel SAT solver frameworks not discussed.
primary_theme: RL-guided logic synthesis for efficient circuit-SAT preprocessing
